title: Introduce capacity mapping and oversubscription safety guardrails
author: Marisol Vega
release_notes: Added a capacity mapping table and oversubscription safety guardrails to improve Dedicated fleet stability under transient load spikes. Includes new telemetry tags and an emergency throttle path. No external API changes.
description:
Motivation: We observed two incidents where per-tenant burst allocations and aggressive oversubscription caused cascading slot pressure in Dedicated pools. This PR introduces an explicit capacity-mapping layer plus conservative oversubscription safety guardrails so the autoscaler and admission path have deterministic behavior under unstable utilization signals.

What this PR does: Adds a capacity_mapping store (in-memory + persisted snapshot) that maps logical tenant commitments to physical pool buckets with a soft- and hard-cap. Introduces an oversubscription_safety policy used by the admission controller and autoscaler to temporarily reject/shed best-effort requests when mapped pool slack falls below a configured watermark. Adds an emergency_throttle path that engages when we detect sustained headroom erosion across a pool for >60s.

Key behavior and knobs: - capacity_mapping: per-tenant entries include committed_units, mapped_pool, mapping_version, and mapping_score. Mapping_score is used by the migrator to rebalance tenants across pools.
- soft_cap_pct: when pool_used >= soft_cap_pct of mapped_capacity we start preferentially routing new bursting traffic to standby pools; this is advisory for autoscaler.
- hard_cap_pct: when pool_used >= hard_cap_pct we reject new burst requests with HTTP 429 and return a Retry-After per tenant policy.
- emergency_throttle_seconds: configured threshold to flip to emergency path (default 60s).

Telemetry & Observability: - new metrics: redwood.capacity_mapping.size, redwood.pool.slack_pct, redwood.oversubscription.events, redwood.emergency_throttle.activations. - span tags: pool_id, tenant_id, mapping_version, throttle_reason. Dashboards updated to include a capacity-mapping heatmap and an oversubscription events chart.

Compatibility & rollout: Behaviour behind feature flag feature.capacity_mapping_v1 for initial canary. Default configuration is conservative (soft_cap_pct=0.75, hard_cap_pct=0.95). Rollout plan: canary on two small Dedicated clusters for 24h, collect slack/activation rates, then progressive ramp to all Dedicated clusters over a week.

Testing: unit tests for mapping table and admission flow; integration tests in perf-lab that simulate tenant-level burst traffic and validate that emergency_throttle prevents pool-wide collapse; added e2e smoke that asserts 429 behavior under sustained overload. Benchmarked the admission check: median p99 latency +0.6ms.

Files changed (summary): config schema additions, autoscaler admission hook, capacity mapping store + snapshotting, metrics + dashboard JSON, feature flag gating, docs for ops.

Related: ENG-7862 (capacity hygiene), ENG-7901 (incident postmortem). SUP-1234 was the support escalation that triggered initial diagnosis.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the oversubscription policy conservative to avoid customer-visible failures; emergency_throttle path prefers safe rejection of best-effort bursts over silent tail-latency amplification. Ops: when investigating activations, check redwood.pool.slack_pct and mapping_version drift.
